The quote for the third clause ("making the switch fabric robust against thermal crosstalk, even in the absence of a cooling system") supports "without chip cooling" but never says feedback control; the word feedback sits in W2327284773's abstract one clause earlier than where this cited quote begins.
"We report on the development of the first ... switch" is a first-demonstration signal word, matching lab; no pilot/production language.
First quote literally says "proof-of-concept in lab", a direct match for lab; the CMOS-foundry fabrication detail is consistent, not contradictory.

Quote says a Mach-Zehnder silicon switch is CMOS-fabricated but never uses waveguide, chip, integrated, or photonic; integrated_photonic here rests on domain knowledge, not words the quote states (same standard applied to mems_3d/mems_2d:integration in round 3).
"Announces today the launch of its new G5" is a product-launch/commercially-available signal, matching production; note already flags it as a vendor claim.
All three clauses map to their quotes: crossing loss growing with ports, control units/wiring growing with ports, and high power consumption attributed to the thermo-optic effect (heater power).
Value is a near-verbatim paraphrase of the quote (MCF collimator, spatial multiplexer/demultiplexer array, LCoS spatial light modulator, integrated in a prototype).
"Successfully fabricated for the first time" is a lab signal word, no pilot/production language.

"World's first large-scale production deployment" and "shipped" are direct, literal matches for production.
